title: Special products
examples: When do I use the special product formulas?
Can you show me an example of (a plus b) cubed?
Is there a pattern when I square a difference?

explain.say: Today we will learn about special products in algebra. These are patterns for expanding certain expressions. We will start with squaring a sum or a difference.
Remember that squaring something means multiplying it by itself. So, (a plus b) squared is just (a plus b) times (a plus b).
When we expand (a plus b) squared, the middle term is always two times a times b. This is a key pattern to remember.
Next we look at (a minus b) squared. This pattern is very similar to the first one. The middle term will have a minus sign.
Finally, we look at cubing a sum, which is (a plus b) cubed. This means (a plus b) times (a plus b) times (a plus b).

faq.q: What is the difference between (a+b)² and a² + b²?
faq.a: When you square a sum, you must include the middle term. The middle term is two times a times b. You might also ask for the expansion of a squared plus b squared.
asks: How do I expand (a plus b) squared?
What is the middle term when squaring a sum?

faq.q: How do I use these formulas to calculate large numbers?
faq.a: You can use them to calculate numbers like ninety-nine squared. It is much easier than multiplying directly. You might also ask how to calculate 99 squared.
asks: Is this useful for calculating squares?

faq.q: Does the sign of the middle term change when I use (a-b)²?
faq.a: Yes, the sign of the middle term changes. For (a minus b) squared, the middle term is negative. You might also ask for the sign in (a-b)².
asks: What is the middle term for (a-b)²?
Does the minus sign affect the middle term?

faq.a: The formula for cubing a sum is a cubed plus three times a squared times b plus three times a times b squared plus b cubed. You might also ask for the expansion of (a+b)³.
asks: What is the expansion of a plus b cubed?

faq.q: Are these formulas only for variables like x and y?
faq.a: No, these formulas work for any numbers you substitute for a and b. You can use them with any values. You might also ask if I can use numbers here.
asks: Can I use numbers in these products?
Do a and b have to be letters?

facts: The expansion of (a plus b) squared is a squared plus two ab plus b squared.
The expansion of (a minus b) squared is a squared minus two ab plus b squared.
The expansion of (a plus b) cubed is a cubed plus three a squared b plus three a b squared plus b cubed.
These formulas help expand binomials quickly without full multiplication.
